chunks: From him, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Sadaqah, from ʿAmmar, from Jaʿfar عليه السلام, from his father.
That ʿAli عليه السلام did not give ghusl to ʿAmmar ibn Yasir nor Hashim ibn ʿUtbah al-Mirqal, and he buried them in their clothes, and did not perform salat over them.
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: His statement, “and he did not perform salat over them,” is an error from the narrator, because salat does not fall from him in any circumstance; that indicates this.

key_terms.ثِيَابِهِمَا: their clothes, meaning they were buried in the garments they wore
key_terms.دَفَنَهُمَا: he buried the two of them
key_terms.وَهْمٌ: an error or mistaken addition by the narrator
key_terms.يَغْسِلْ: to wash ritually, meaning to give the deceased ghusl
key_terms.يُصَلِّ: to perform salat, here referring to funeral prayer
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةَ: the funeral salat in this context

ai.seo_question: Did Imam ʿAli عليه السلام perform funeral salat over martyrs buried in their clothes?
ai.summary: This report states that Imam ʿAli عليه السلام did not wash two martyrs and buried them in their clothes. Shaykh al-Tusi then clarifies that the phrase stating he did not perform salat over them is a mistake by the narrator, because the funeral salat is not omitted in such a case. The passage therefore relates both a historical report and a juristic correction regarding burial rites.
